leads.title: Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968-69 (Bill C-150)
leads.documents: Decriminalization of same-sex sexual activity in private between consenting adults in Canada, applicable in Nova Scotia; foundational legal status
leads.detail: Cited as brought into force upon royal assent June 27, 1969; introduced 1967 by Justice Minister Pierre Trudeau. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms - Section 15(1), Section 1, Section 33
leads.documents: Constitutional equality guarantee, reasonable limits (Oakes Test), and notwithstanding clause framework for LGBTQ protections and enforcement machinery
leads.detail: Quotes s.15(1) text; notes s.15 came into force 1985; discusses Oakes Test and s.33 use in Saskatchewan and Alberta gender/education laws. No URL visible.

leads.title: Egan v. Canada, Supreme Court of Canada (1995)
leads.documents: Landmark ruling that sexual orientation is protected under s.15 equality clause as analogous ground
leads.detail: Cited as 1995 landmark decision. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Vriend v Alberta, Supreme Court of Canada (1998)
leads.documents: Failure of provincial legislature to include sexual orientation in human rights law is itself s.15 violation; basis for all provinces/territories + federal inclusion by 2017 of sexual orientation and gender identity
leads.detail: Cited as 1998 decision; notes as of 2017 all jurisdictions explicitly include sexual orientation and gender identity. No URL visible.

leads.title: Civil Marriage Act (Federal, 2005) + Supreme Court Reference (2004) and Provincial Marriage Cases 2002-2005
leads.documents: Nationwide legalization of same-sex marriage; Ontario Court of Appeal immediate effect, followed by other provinces; federal non-appeal 2003
leads.detail: Parliament passed July 20, 2005; Supreme Court declared proposed definition consistent with Charter Dec 2004; Canada 4th country worldwide, 1st in Americas. No URL visible.

leads.title: Criminal Code Section 159 and repeal via Bill C-32 / Bill C-75
leads.documents: Former anal intercourse offence with unequal age provision; declared unconstitutional by courts in Ontario, Quebec, British Columbia, Nova Scotia, and Alberta; repealed to equalize age of consent at 16
leads.detail: Nova Scotia court specifically cited as declaring s.159 unconstitutional; Bill C-32 introduced Nov 15, 2016, incorporated into C-75 tabled March 2018, royal assent June 21, 2019. Statement by MP Randy Boissonnault quoted. No URL visible.

leads.title: Expungement of Historically Unjust Convictions Act + Parole Board of Canada statement
leads.documents: Government report/legal remedy allowing destruction/removal of RCMP/federal records for pre-1969 homosexual acts and s.159 convictions; distinguishes expungement vs pardon
leads.detail: Royal assent June 21, 2018; requires notification to provincial/municipal police and courts; Parole Board states expungement available to living and deceased. No URL visible.

leads.title: Canadian Association of Chiefs of Police apology - December 2020
leads.documents: National law-enforcement admission of decades of oppression, institutional bias, and human rights violations against 2SLGBTQ+ from 1960s to present; creation of Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Committee
leads.detail: Quoted apology issued on International Day of Human Rights 2020. No URL visible.

leads.title: Asher & Lyric LGBTQ+ Danger Index 2023, Gay Travel Index 2024, Equaldex Equality Index 2024
leads.documents: Institutional safety rankings documenting Canada as most gay-friendly/least dangerous (1st in 2023 Danger Index, 1st in 2024 Gay Travel Index, 9th Equaldex 2024) - direct visitor-safety indicator for Nova Scotia
leads.detail: Titles/years/ranks as cited in lead. No URL visible.

leads.title: Nova Scotia same-sex adoption legalization (2001) / Privy Council Office poll (2020) and Pew Research (2020)
leads.documents: Nova Scotia-specific rights machinery: joint/stepchild adoption by same-sex couples legal since 2001; plus government social-acceptance data: 91.8% comfortable with gay neighbour, 87.6% with transgender neighbour; Pew 85% acceptance (92% age 18-29)
leads.detail: Adoption list cites Nova Scotia (2001) after BC 1996, Ontario 1999; polls cited as June 2013 and 2020 Privy Council Office-commissioned poll. No URL visible.
